imagePullSecrets.description: also given to the DaosSystem's pods unless system.spec.imagePullSecrets is set

metricsBindAddress.description: --metrics-bind-address for the operator's own controller-runtime metrics ("0" = off)

metrics.description: Managed Service for the operator endpoint. HTTPS + Kubernetes auth by default.

defaultImage.description: image the operator uses when DaosSystem.spec.images.hostPrep is empty ("" = daos-hostprep next to image.repository with the operator's tag, e.g. ghcr.io/gluesys/daos-hostprep:<appVersion>)

hostprep.description: ClusterRole "daos-hostprep" that the operator binds to the per-system hostprep ServiceAccount.

enabled.description: ConfigMap with the upstream DAOS Grafana dashboard, labelled for the grafana sidecar

spec.description: DaosSystem spec, passed through as-is and validated by the CRD

system.description: Create one DaosSystem with the release. spec is passed through as-is (see api/v1alpha1 for the fields); the operator fills status.

metrics.description: Provisioner operation duration/errors; not the DAOS data path.

tls.description: mount <system>-certs (agent set for the sidecar, admin set for the daos client)

nodeSelector.description: nodes that may mount DAOS PVs (default: all)

deletionPolicy.description: Delete destroys the DAOS snapshot with the VolumeSnapshot; Retain keeps it (and its space)

snapshots.description: CSI snapshots (VolumeSnapshot). Each snapshot is a DaosContainerSnapshot taken by the operator. A PVC restored from one (dataSource: VolumeSnapshot) with ReadOnlyMany mounts the snapshot itself; any other access mode gets a new container that a restore Job fills from the snapshot (DaosContainer spec.restoreFrom, POSIX containers only). DAOS 2.8 cannot roll a container back in place. Needs the VolumeSnapshot CRDs and snapshot-controller (kubernetes-csi/external-snapshotter), installed once per cluster, and a daos-csi image with snapshot support.

expansion.description: PVC expansion: a csi-resizer sidecar and allowVolumeExpansion on the StorageClasses. Growing a PVC moves its DaosContainer's spec.spaceLimit, which is a container quota in the extended edition of DAOS; on upstream DAOS it only records the size (capacity is per pool). Needs a daos-csi with EXPAND_VOLUME.

storageClasses.description: StorageClasses to create, one per DaosPool

csi.description: exastor/daos-csi: CSI driver (controller Deployment + node DaemonSet with a daos_agent sidecar). One driver per DaosSystem: csi.system names the system whose <system>-agent ConfigMap (and <system>-certs when tls) the node plugin uses.

ibvDrivers.description: IBV_DRIVERS for injected containers: bundled rdma-core providers without the -rdmav<N>.so suffix

rdmaResources.description: extended resources that give a container an RDMA device (a trailing / matches a prefix)

defaultPodSecurity.description: - rdma/ - nvidia.com/hostdev The cluster's default Pod Security enforce level (privileged | baseline | restricted), used for namespaces without a pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce label. Empty = unknown: then the agent socket hostPath is only added to pods that already pass as privileged (hostNetwork, hostPath, privileged), and other pods in unlabelled namespaces are skipped.

excludeNamespaces.description: Namespaces the webhook never sees (the release namespace and kube-system are always excluded)

interception.description: Interception library injection (doc/plans/2026-11-19-client-interception.md). A mutating webhook preloads libioil or libpil4dfs into pods that mount a csi DAOS volume and ask for it with the pod annotation daos.gluesys.com/interception: ioil | pil4dfs | off (or the same label on their namespace as a default), so their I/O bypasses dfuse. Only pods that can be DAOS clients themselves get it: the agent's network side (hostNetwork for RDMA) and, for RDMA, a device (privileged, a /dev/infiniband hostPath, or a resource in rdmaResources). Two init containers copy the bundle from the daos-client image and test-load it in the application's own image; an image that cannot load it (glibc < 2.34, musl) runs on dfuse as before. The operator keeps the webhook's certificate itself (no cert-manager). Needs csi.enabled and a daos-client image with /opt/daos-il (daos-images !11 or later).

pools.description: DaosPools to create, each optionally with the StorageClass that provisions into it. DAOS enforces capacity per pool, not per container: a PVC's requested size is not a limit, and every PVC in a pool shares the pool's size. To give teams or uses their own capacity, give each its own pool and StorageClass here. When a pool passes its spaceWarningPercent the operator sets SpaceLow on the DaosPool and also records a PoolSpaceLow Event on each bound PVC in it, so namespace users see it too. Pools are kept on helm uninstall (resource-policy: keep); destroying one needs the daos.gluesys.com/destroy-approved annotation, as for any DaosPool.

vllm.description: vLLM serving with LMCache writing its KV cache to a DAOS container. This is a reference workload for PoCs, demos and tests -- not part of the storage layer and not a way to run inference in production. It is here so a GPU cluster can be brought up with one release. Production serving (KServe, llm-d, Dynamo, ...) follows the integration contract in doc/serving-integration.md; verified combinations are in doc/compatibility.md. See also doc/deploy-gpu-k8s.md. The pod runs with hostNetwork because a DAOS client must be reachable at the address it advertises; a pod-network client behind the CNI's masquerade is not (that is also why spec.clientAgent must be enabled on the GPU nodes). rdma: true is needed when DAOS runs on an RDMA provider (ofi+verbs and the like): without /dev/infiniband the client pod cannot initialise the libfabric verbs provider. On a cluster with an RDMA device plugin, prefer rdmaResource over rdma. The plugin injects only the verbs devices the pod asks for, which drops both the /dev/infiniband hostPath and privileged and leaves IPC_LOCK, at the same speed -- measured on 400G RoCE, 64 MiB round trip: 2777 MB/s write, 12162 MB/s read. If both are set, rdmaResource wins. rdmaResource: rdma/rdma_shared_device_a   # the name the NVIDIA Network Operator advertises rdmaResourceCount: 1 The vllm-lmcache-daos image in the example below lives in our internal registry only -- at 10 GB we do not mirror it publicly. The build recipe is public, so build your own: images/vllm-lmcache-daos/ in github.com/gluesys/daos-images.

s3.description: S3 gateways (versitygw-daos) in front of a DaosPool, one S3Service per entry. The operator supplies --pool/--system, the daos_agent sidecar and the certificates; see doc/adr/ADR-004-s3-gateway.md. The versitygw-daos image lives in our internal registry only: it carries a fork whose source is not public, so we do not mirror it. The build recipe is public: images/versitygw/ in github.com/gluesys/daos-images.
